facts.statement: Texas HHS says nonemergency medical transportation can include public transportation, taxi or van service, and commercial transit for eligible covered health care; some users may qualify for gas assistance.
facts.operationalNote: Users should follow their health plan or HHSC instructions and verify current scheduling requirements before travel.

facts.statement: Texas DSHS and HRSA use Health Professional Shortage Area and Medically Underserved Area/Population designations for primary care, dental and mental-health shortage planning.
facts.operationalNote: Designation status can affect eligibility for some workforce programs and should be checked at the official source.

facts.statement: Texas DSHS has published 2026-27 school and childcare immunization requirement materials, including bilingual resources.
facts.operationalNote: Use the current school-year documents; do not rely on cached summaries for compliance decisions.

facts.statement: CMS hospital price-transparency requirements changed for calendar year 2026, including additional allowed-amount data elements in machine-readable files.
facts.operationalNote: Published hospital prices support comparison but do not guarantee a patient's final out-of-pocket bill.

facts.statement: CDC heat guidance recommends planning for proper medication storage and powered medical devices during heat and outages and advises against changing medications without clinician guidance.
facts.operationalNote: Individual plans belong with the prescribing clinician, pharmacist and device manufacturer guidance.

facts.statement: TxDOT states that public transportation programs help people in rural areas access health care and that Section 5310 supports mobility for seniors and people with disabilities in eligible areas.
facts.operationalNote: Service availability varies by locality and provider.
